newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC denies tariff waiver to NSP.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC denies tariff waiver to NSP.

text.p: U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday denied a request from Northern States Power Co for a waiver from filing a new open access transmission tariff.

Under the commission's new rules promoting competition among power producers, all public utilities which own transmission lines must file new tariffs offering the same service on the same terms to all power producers as the utilities provide themselves.
NSP had sought a waiver, saying its transmission tariffs filed before the new rules came into effect on July 10 met the requirements. But the commission said they were inadequate.
The commission issued the ruling on NSP's request along with action on 29 other waiver requests.
It denied waivers to 18 utilities, including Madison Gas & Electric Co, which could receive requests for transmission service in the future, even if they did not already serve other power producers.

It granted waivers to 11 entities which are owned by other utilities or created to run a specific project, but told seven of them they would have to file open access tariffs if they received a request for service.

The commission also granted 21 waivers to its rule requiring transmission owners to set up electronic information systems giving all customers equal access to information about transmission availability at all times.
